title: Crimes under the Special and Local Laws (SLL) 1 18.1 The crime head-wise incidence and rate of cognizable crimes under the Special and Local Laws (SLL) during 1987 and 1992 to 1996 are presented in Table-10. The quinquennial average of incidence and rate for the period 1992-96 as also the percentage variations during 1997 over 1987, Q.A. and over the previous year (1996) are also presented in this table. 1.18.2 During 1997, a total of 46,91,439 cognizable crimes were reported in the country under various Special Laws and Local Laws. These incidents showed a steady increase, with 30.7 per cent over the decade 1987-97, 15.6 per cent over the Q.A. of 1992-96 and 2.3 per cent over the previous year (1996). 1.18.3 The crime head-wise percentage distribution of various cognizable crimes under the SLL during the last 5 years (1952 to 1996) is presented in Table-11. It is observed that the 21 specified crimes heads accounted for one-fifth (21.4%) of the total SLL crimes, while the remaining 78.6 per cent were clubbed as “Over SLL crimes”. The “Prohibition Act” and “Excise Act”, though enforced in only a few States, were a major contributor with 14.0 per cent have toward and SLL crimes. Next in order were the “Gambling Act” (2.5%) and the “Arms Act” (1.6%). Each of the remaining 17 specified crimes contributed less than 1 per cent and together accounted for the 2.3 per cent of the total SLL crimes.
